name: Ife heads and the National Museum of Ife
subtitle: Artisans in Ife made heads in copper alloy (widely called bronze) and terracotta with a highly symmetrical style.

facts.label: What
facts.value: Ife heads, whether metal or terracotta, share a highly symmetrical style.

facts.label: Date and place
facts.value: The National Geographic caption dates a bronze Ooni head in the National Museum of Ife to the 12th-15th century.

facts.label: Date
facts.value: The most significant find of Ife heads occurred in 1938, when more than a dozen were found.

facts.label: Where kept
facts.value: Many of the 1938 heads can be seen today in Ife's Museum of Antiquities.

facts.label: Who they depict
facts.value: Study has shown that the regal heads depict men, the ooni (rulers of Yoruba kingdoms), not gods.

facts.label: Meaning
facts.value: In Yoruba belief the head is the home of the Ori, the seat of the soul and where a person's fate is determined.

facts.label: Terracotta
facts.value: Numerous terracotta heads were unearthed from ritual resting places and many were taken to museums.

facts.label: Change or risk
facts.value: Many Nigerians are advocating for the repatriation of the Ife heads.

parts.text: Artisans in Ife made heads in copper alloy (widely called bronze) and terracotta with a highly symmetrical style. A find of more than a dozen metal heads in 1938 is the most significant, and many can be seen today in Ife's Museum of Antiquities. Study has shown the heads depict ooni, rulers of Yoruba kingdoms, not gods.
